[1/3] Plan: make post exposure and vignette per-scene settings (defaults 1.12 and 0.28), persist them through snapshots, scene export and editor set_scene, report them in renderer stats, and keep the canonical frame identical

impact_assessment.why: The tonemap was configurable but exposure and vignette stayed compile-time constants, so games could not tune grade brightness or corner falloff and AI clients could not diff them.
impact_assessment.benefits: Authorable grade controls from Python, snapshots and the editor, visible in reports, with defaults that preserve every existing frame.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: two PostSettings fields, scene export schema 4 and editor schema 61; dependency: none; concurrency: none; state: additive snapshot fields with defaults.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Validate ranges at construction/editor/load, pin rendered brightness and corner darkening, keep defaults equal to the constants, and run strict gates.

checkpoints.description: [2/3] Implemented and verified - PostSettings.exposure (finite, non-negative, default 1.12) and vignette (0..1, default 0.28) validate; the renderer, sky and sprite passes read scene values and stats report post_exposure/post_vignette; snapshots, scene export (schema 4), editor document/set_scene (schema 61) carry both; CPU defaults match POST_EXPOSURE/POST_VIGNETTE; exposure 2.0 renders brighter and vignette 1.0 darkens the corner while 0.0 does not; disable post still ignores both; 1272 tests green, ruff clean, aikit check keystone 6/6 gates, canonical hash 772cac5232a0947b8f6d1914a5cf0cde and 4899-byte reference PNG unchanged; checklists: passed
Task 'keystone-grade-controls-v1' completed successfully.

[1/3] Plan: add opt-in FXAA as PostSettings.anti_alias, implemented as a full-screen luma-edge pass over the scene/composite FBO, persisted through snapshots, scene export and editor set_scene, reported in stats, and leaving the default path byte-identical

impact_assessment.why: Geometry edges were hard aliased and anti-aliasing was the last named post-chain item; the bloom color FBOs already exist, so FXAA needs one program and one extra full-res target when bloom is off.
impact_assessment.benefits: Opt-in edge smoothing for silhouettes and high-contrast edges, authorable from Python and the editor, visible in reports, with no change to existing frames.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: PostSettings field, render path branches, scene export schema 5, editor schema 62; dependency: none; concurrency: none; state: additive snapshot field.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Keep the no-AA/no-bloom direct path untouched, compose bloom into _post_fbo before resolving, test silhouette changes and a uniform-frame no-op, and verify the canonical frame unchanged.

checkpoints.description: [2/3] Implemented and verified - PostSettings.anti_alias (none/fxaa) validates; FXAA_FRAGMENT runs as a full-screen luma-edge pass; render routes through _bloom_scene when bloom or FXAA is on, blooms into _post_fbo when both are on, and resolves to the default framebuffer; the no-AA/no-bloom path is unchanged; snapshots, scene export (schema 5), editor set_scene (schema 62) and stats (post_aa) carry it; a rotated cube changes pixels with FXAA, a uniform frame does not, and bloom+FXAA composes; 1278 tests green, ruff clean, aikit check keystone 6/6 gates, canonical hash 772cac5232a0947b8f6d1914a5cf0cde and 4899-byte reference PNG unchanged; checklists: passed
Task 'keystone-fxaa-v1' completed successfully.

[1/3] Plan: add inspect_navgrid and bake_navgrid editor actions so navigation authoring matches the tile-map loop, with schema examples/fields, document exposure, argument validation and no scene mutation

impact_assessment.why: Nav grids were derivable and persistable in Python but unreachable from the JSON authoring surface; tile maps had just gained inspect/build, leaving navigation inconsistent.
impact_assessment.benefits: An AI can bake a grid from the live scene, receive the schema-1 document, validate documents, and persist exactly what it measured.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: two editor actions, editor fields and schema entries; dependency: web server imports nav_authoring and pathfinding; concurrency: session lock; state: one-shot fields reset per action and baking adds no undo step.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Validate width/height/origin/layer/clearance before baking, return counts plus the document, pin the document round trip and four error paths, and keep the canonical frame unchanged.

checkpoints.description: [2/3] Implemented and verified - inspect_navgrid validates a schema-1 document and reports width/height/blocked/free; bake_navgrid parses width/height/cell_size/origin/clearance/layer, bakes scene_boxes through grid_from_boxes, and returns counts, settings, box count and the schema-1 document; both are registered with schema examples and fields and exposed as navgrid/navgrid_bake in the editor document; README, ARCHITECTURE, CHANGELOG and ADR-248 updated; a 6x6 bake reports blocked >= 1 and its document round-trips through NavGrid.from_dict; invalid width, two-element origin, blank layer and negative clearance return 400; 1279 tests green, ruff clean, aikit check keystone 6/6 gates, canonical hash 772cac5232a0947b8f6d1914a5cf0cde and 4899-byte reference PNG unchanged; checklists: passed
Task 'keystone-editor-navgrid-v1' completed successfully.
[1/3] Plan: add route_navgrid to the editor API, running A* with optional diagonals and smoothing on a schema-1 document and returning the report, raw route and smoothed route under navgrid_route

impact_assessment.why: The editor could bake and inspect nav grids but not ask for a route, so an AI could not verify connectivity from the same JSON surface.
impact_assessment.benefits: The bake-inspect-route loop closes, letting an AI prove a level is traversable and choose between raw and smoothed routes.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: one editor action, editor field and schema entries; dependency: web server imports pathfinding helpers; concurrency: session lock; state: one-shot result resets per action.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Validate cells and flags before routing, return not-found for unreachable goals, pin wall detour, diagonal cost and five error paths, and keep the canonical frame unchanged.

checkpoints.description: [2/3] Implemented and verified - route_navgrid validates a schema-1 grid plus integer start/goal pairs and boolean diagonal/smooth flags, runs find_path, smooths a found route, and exposes report, raw route, smoothed route and flags as navgrid_route; registered in EDITOR_ACTIONS with schema example and fields; README, ARCHITECTURE, CHANGELOG and ADR-249 updated; a 5x3 wall routes around it, a 5x5 diagonal costs four sqrt(2), a walled column returns found false with an empty smoothed route, and five malformed payloads return 400; 1280 tests green, ruff clean, aikit check keystone 6/6 gates, canonical hash 772cac5232a0947b8f6d1914a5cf0cde and 4899-byte reference PNG unchanged; checklists: passed
Task 'keystone-editor-navroute-v1' completed successfully.

[1/3] Plan: add a composed NavAgent over A*, smoothing, waypoint following, steering and CharacterController, with explicit set_goal/replan/step, JSON-safe progress, obstacle and neighbour avoidance, and discovery

impact_assessment.why: The navigation pieces exist separately; games and AI authors still wire them in the right order, derive the start cell, and manage replanning, which is the NavMeshAgent-shaped gap.
impact_assessment.benefits: One object turns a goal cell into movement with collision and avoidance, while keeping the body decoupled from a scene node and reporting progress.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: new module, two exports and a capability; dependency: nav_agent imports character, navigation, pathfinding, steering; concurrency: agent state is caller-owned; state: no schema change.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Validate all inputs, plan once on set_goal with explicit replan, clear unreachable plans, keep separation optional, prove a full wall detour plus immediate arrival, and keep the canonical evidence unchanged.

checkpoints.description: [1/3] Plan (impact-assessed): add a composed NavAgent over A*, smoothing, waypoint following, steering and CharacterController with explicit set_goal/replan/step, JSON-safe progress and optional neighbour avoidance

impact_assessment.why: The navigation pieces exist separately; games still wire them in the right order, derive the start cell and manage replanning, which is the NavMeshAgent-shaped gap.
impact_assessment.benefits: One object turns a goal cell into movement with collision and avoidance while keeping the body decoupled from a scene node and reporting progress.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: new module, two exports and a capability; dependency: nav_agent imports character, navigation, pathfinding and steering; concurrency: agent state is caller-owned; state: no schema change.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Validate all inputs, plan once on set_goal with explicit replan, clear unreachable plans, keep separation optional, prove a full wall detour plus immediate arrival, and keep the canonical evidence unchanged.

checkpoints.description: [2/3] Implemented and verified - keystone/nav_agent.py adds NavAgent and nav_agent_report; set_goal derives the start cell, plans, smooths, converts points and installs a follower; unreachable clears the plan, blocked or outside goals raise; replan reruns; step validates dt, advances by reported position, optionally avoids NavAgent neighbours via steering, steps the controller, clears the goal on arrival and returns a schema-1 report; a 6x6 wall detour reaches the goal grounded, self-cell goals finish immediately, neighbour avoidance changes advance while zero weight does not; exports, README section and bullet, ARCHITECTURE row and tree, docs/TREE, CHANGELOG and ADR-250 updated; --describe reports capabilities.nav_agent; 13 tests green (1293 collected), ruff clean, aikit check keystone 6/6 gates, canonical hash 772cac5232a0947b8f6d1914a5cf0cde and 4899-byte reference PNG unchanged; checklists: passed
Task 'keystone-nav-agent-v1' completed successfully.

[1/3] Plan: add trace_navgrid to the editor API, walking a fresh NavAgent from start to goal under a frame budget and reporting found/reached/steps plus the final body state, closing the bake-inspect-route-walk authoring chain

impact_assessment.why: A legal route is not a traversal; an AI could not verify that a controller-driven agent actually reaches a goal through the JSON surface.
impact_assessment.benefits: One action proves walkability with the real agent stack, without mutating the scene or leaving state behind.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: one editor action, editor field and schema entries; dependency: web server imports nav_agent, character and physics; concurrency: session lock; state: ephemeral trace only.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Validate all numbers and cells, cap the frame budget, use a safe floor height, report unreachable without stepping, pin success and failure traces, and keep the canonical frame unchanged.

checkpoints.description: [2/3] Implemented and verified - trace_navgrid parses a schema-1 grid, integer start/goal cells, finite cell_size/origin/height/speed/dt and a bounded frame budget, builds a fresh CharacterBody at the start cell centre, walks a NavAgent over a floor AABB, and reports found, steps, reached and the final nav_agent_report; unreachable goals report found false with zero steps; registered in EDITOR_ACTIONS with schema example and fields, exposed as navgrid_trace, and documented in README/ARCHITECTURE/CHANGELOG and ADR-251; the 5x3 wall trace reaches x > 4.2 grounded while the walled column does not, and six malformed payloads return 400; 1294 tests green, ruff clean, aikit check keystone 6/6 gates, canonical hash 772cac5232a0947b8f6d1914a5cf0cde and 4899-byte reference PNG unchanged; checklists: passed
Task 'keystone-editor-navgride-trace-v1' completed successfully.
